expectations.text: The plan gate is evaluated against all three loop-readiness properties before any round runs
expectations.evidence: Before the first dispatch, the run only listed and read files and ran a baseline `make check`, then went straight to the "Implement farewell helper (section 1)" subagent, with no plan-gate evaluation of named sections, the ticked-checkbox contract, or section-scoped checks. The run's own notes confirm "`/factory` is not in the available skills list... I used my own workflow."
expectations.rubric: Before any round runs, the plan gate must be evaluated against all three loop-readiness properties (named sections, ticked-checkbox contract, section-scoped checks). This is a process assertion read from the transcript.

expectations.text: Exactly three new commits land, one per section, each in Conventional Commits format
Each section's checkboxes are ticked in that section's own commit

Each round dispatches a fresh subagent to the role its annotation selects, the sai-hu-annotated section going to sai-hu on the first round noted as per annotation, and no dispatch passes a model or effort parameter
expectations.evidence: Both dispatches passed a model parameter (`subagent_type=general-purpose, model=sonnet` for sections 1 and 3), and section 2 was done inline ("I did section 2 myself") with no fresh subagent. The `sai-hu` section was not dispatched to `sai-hu` or recorded per annotation or in fallback form; it was only noted that "Neither is an available agent type, so I used the substitute".
expectations.rubric: Each round must run in a fresh subagent dispatched to the role the section's annotation selects: the sai-hu-annotated section goes to sai-hu on the first round (noted per annotation), the default-annotated sections to too-te, and no dispatch may pass a model or effort parameter. In a rosterless harness where the role types are not installed and a dispatch to them would fail, dispatching a fresh general subagent that carries the intended role's one-line contract and recording the role in the ledger in fallback form (for example `sai-hu (fallback: general)`) counts as honoring the annotation; a bare without_skill arm does not invent these fallback annotations on its own, so the assertion still discriminates. Reading which role each round used (or its fallback form), whether the sai-hu section was honored on the first round, and whether any model or effort parameter was passed is a judgment over the round reports.

expectations.text: Dispatch is exactly one subagent deep: rounds dispatch, and no dispatched subagent spawns another
expectations.evidence: The main session made exactly two `[tool:Agent]` dispatches ("Implement farewell helper (section 1)" and "Implement shout helper (section 3)", both `general-purpose`, `sonnet`). The tool calls shown between each dispatch and its hand-back are only shell commands and a Read, with no further Agent call, so dispatch occurred and stayed one level deep.
expectations.rubric: Dispatch annotations select a starting role, never a nested delegation: no round's subagent may spawn a further subagent. Requires reasoning over the dispatch structure in the transcript. The property is dispatched-but-flat, so this row is NOT vacuously satisfied by the mere absence of nesting: if the run dispatched no subagent at all (it executed the sections inline in the main session), mark it failed, not passed. Pass only when at least one round dispatched a subagent AND no dispatched subagent spawned another.

expectations.text: A one-line round report is emitted for every round, and a final ledger whose per-round lines name each section's role and any marker (per annotation, escalated, or turn budget) appears with per-round durations and total wall time
expectations.evidence: The final reply is a three-sentence prose summary with no ledger, per-round durations or total wall time; the table written to outputs/result.md has only "Round | Section | Done by | Failing test first | `make check` after" columns, with no durations or wall time, and only Round 2 has anything like a one-line "Round 2 result" report in the transcript.
expectations.rubric: Every round emits a one-line report, and the run closes with a ledger where each round's line names the section's role and any marker (per annotation, escalated, or turn budget) alongside per-round durations and a total wall time. Presence and completeness of the ledger, including the per-round role and marker, is a structural judgment on the reply.

expectations.text: /opsx:verify is recorded as unavailable, not simulated as passing
expectations.evidence: Neither the final reply nor the run's written transcript.md/result.md mentions `/opsx:verify`; they report only that `/factory`, the `too-te`/`sai-hu` agents and the `openspec` CLI were unavailable. No pass was fabricated, but `/opsx:verify` was never recorded as unavailable.
expectations.rubric: /opsx:verify must be recorded as unavailable rather than simulated as passing. Distinguishing an honest 'unavailable' note from a fabricated pass requires reading intent, not one string match.
